requirements.expected: With no search, category, type, color, Favorites, or explicit alternate sort active, the main Prompt Kit library renders prompts in ascending numeric sequence. Recommendation ranking may affect recommendation results but must not globally replace the library's chronological sequence order.
Every filtered visible prompt set preserves ascending numeric prompt sequence, allowing gaps and never renumbering stable prompt IDs.
The rendered visible prompt stream exposes both Top and Bottom navigation at intervals of no more than five visible prompt cards. A final partial group also retains navigation access.

Distributed Top and Bottom controls are created inside the canonical render path from the current visible result set, so every search, category, type, color, Favorites, or other filter rerender reconstructs navigation without clearing filter state.

The distributed navigation helper creates same-document Top and Bottom anchors using the page-jump class, and CSS associated specifically with distributed navigation supplies at least a 40px mobile/coarse-pointer touch target. Native anchors preserve keyboard access.
Every canonical prompt has a unique P-number ID and unique numeric sequence whose numeric values match; chronological display ordering never renumbers those stable ID/sequence identities.

The tracked web/prompt-kit/index.html exactly matches scripts/build_prompt_kit_registry.py render output, so order/navigation evidence is evaluated against the same deterministic product surface that is delivered.

evidence: scripts/build_prompt_kit_registry.py preserves discoveryRank metadata but returns the canonical registry in ascending numeric seq order.
docs/prompt-kit-guided-recommendations.js keeps recommendation rank local to questionnaire results and no longer overrides the main library sequence function.
docs/prompt-kit.js sorts the complete filtered card stream numerically, exposes Favorites as an explicit filter, and renders each category divider at most once.
docs/prompt-kit.js reconstructs Top and Bottom navigation after every five actually rendered prompt cards plus the final partial group from inside render().
The strict validator proves canonical site parity and canonical ID/sequence integrity before reporting implementation pass.

proof_ceiling: Contract registration, canonical registry identity checks, exact generated-site parity, and static source evidence can prove the requirement and detect implementation regressions. Static checks do not prove real scrolling ergonomics, touch behavior, browser focus, or mobile acceptance; those require observed browser/device proof.
